title: Lightning Distance Histogram by Storm
dataSources: Seismograph events (`seismograph:event`), seismic noise (`seismograph:noise`), air quality (`airquality:reading`), radiation counts (`radiation:count`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), phenology observations (`phenology:observation`), and weather-station rainfall (`weatherstation:reading`).
app: Citizen-science telemetry from seismographs, weather stations, air-quality monitors, Geiger counters, lightning feeds, and phenology journals streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=lightning:strike
| eval distance_bucket_km=ceil(distance_km/5)*5
| stats count as strikes by storm_id distance_bucket_km
| sort storm_id distance_bucket_km
description: Buckets lightning strikes by distance for each storm so approach patterns are easy to compare.
value: Distance histograms make a lightning feed feel less abstract by showing whether storms brushed past or came directly overhead.
implementation: Capture strike distance and a storm identifier from Blitzortung or your lightning sensor integration.
visualization: Histogram of strike counts by distance bucket for each storm.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how close each storm's lightning usually got, so nearby storms are easier to compare.
